documents.content:
06:10 – Arrived on site. Walked the Main Electrical Panel (Panel A) and stage dimmer racks. No overnight alarms in the panel log. Ambient temp in the electrical room 78°F, slightly warm but within normal range.

06:25 – Stage 2 house lights flickered once during generator transfer test (scheduled, per facilities email). Noted in passing; no action needed. Transfer switch operated normally, returned to utility power in 4 sec.

06:40 – Checked exterior lot receptacles per request from grip dept. Receptacle EX-7 cover plate was loose. Tightened cover screws. No load issue. Receptacle voltage 121V, within tolerance.

07:05 – Main Electrical Panel: recorded line-to-line voltages. A-B: 208.4V, B-C: 208.1V, A-C: 208.6V. Line-to-neutral on each leg: 120.2V, 120.0V, 120.4V. All within ±3% of nominal. Load amperage on main breaker was 412A at time of reading (normal for morning setup, usually 380–450A).

07:20 – Replaced burnt-out work light in Stage 1 catwalk (fixture #C-14). Used 500W tungsten, same as spec. Logged in maintenance book.

07:45 – Grip dept reported intermittent hum in dimmer rack 2, channel 12. Checked dimmer curve and module. Found loose phoenix connector on output terminal. Re-seated connector, tightened to 5 in-lb. Hum stopped. No parts replaced.

08:15 – Routine check of generator room. Fuel level 78%. Oil pressure and coolant temp normal. Started gen for 5 min per weekly exercise schedule. No fault codes. Returned to auto standby.

08:40 – Main Electrical Panel breaker_tripped main_breaker. Record status: current. At approximately 08:37, production assistant called to say the entire building lost power. I was in the generator room and heard the panel open (loud bang). Went to the electrical room. Found the main breaker in the Main Electrical Panel in the tripped position. No visible arc damage, no burn smell, no scorch marks on the panel face or bus bars. Reset the main breaker after verifying with a clamp meter that there was no dead short on the load side (phase-to-phase and phase-to-ground readings all open). Re-energized at 08:44. Building power restored. All dimmer racks and distros came back up normally. Noted that the breaker felt warm to the touch on the handle, but not hot. Panel room temp 81°F at time of reset.

09:10 – After reset, took a full set of readings on the Main Electrical Panel. Voltages: A-B 208.2V, B-C 208.0V, A-C 208.5V. Load amperage on main breaker: 396A and steady. No unusual harmonics on the phase monitor. Checked all sub-panels (SP-1, SP-2, SP-3) for tripped breakers – none. All branch breakers in normal position.

09:35 – Called the production office to report the trip. Spoke to Casey in facilities. Left a note on their desk with the time and readings. Recommended a thermal scan of the main breaker and panel bus if the trip repeats. No further action taken this shift.

09:50 – Walked the building to confirm all equipment was back on line. Found the craft services coffee maker in the green room had tripped its own GFCI (unrelated to main breaker trip). Reset GFCI. Coffee maker back on.

10:15 – Checked stage 2 generator transfer switch again per Casey's request. Operated manually and auto. Both fine. No alarms.

10:40 – Replaced a blown fuse in the sound stage wall box (SB-3, 20A, time-delay). Fuse was old, no markings on the glass. Replaced with same rating. Noted in the fuse inventory sheet.

11:00 – Lunch break.

11:30 – Returned from lunch. Checked the Main Electrical Panel log for any additional alarms since 08:44. None. Load amperage 388A. Voltages stable.
